findings.reason: the numbers state what the change must move, and an unmeasurable 8%-of-a-partial-tick figure either promises an improvement the endpoint cannot deliver or is discarded by whoever builds the gate, leaving the node's success undefined.
findings.text: the Why opens on a 4-7 minute tick against a 10 s target and then gives the read two incompatible shares: "half the samples doing reckon work" (counting only reckon samples) and "8% of the tick" from a 60 s profile at 20:30Z, which samples a fraction of a 4-7 minute tick and, per the sibling record at docs/plans/the-monitor-tells-the-truth-under-load.html:227 ("reckon-96 and reckon-56 each profiled the station that evening and could attribute only the active samples, not the time each stage spent"), cannot attribute stage time at all — so the plan claims a tick-time share its instrument does not measure; a worker closing the node cannot tell whether it must move 8% of one stage or the 4-7 minute figure

findings.reason: a worker will run the row-bound measure against a read shape where the bound is unsatisfiable by the stated endpoint and must either narrow the read and change the fleet-width figure or weaken the assertion so it can no longer fail, which is the defect the section exists to prevent.
findings.text: "an activity-bounded read" names no read shape, and at base the same parameter bounds nothing on the figures path: reckon/ledger.py:4011-4012 says "Figures use a narrow timestamp projection across all plans to count width", and reckon/ledger.py:4053 loads that projection through stored_run_rows over the project's whole history before selection, so the row-count endpoint is unreachable for read_records(activity_since=...) at its default with_figures=True, while the station's own read passes with_figures=False (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4041)

findings.reason: as written the worker must either force a base-equality test to fail (impossible without inventing a fault) or leave "each" unmet, so the gate cannot be read as a proof of the failing-first arms.
findings.text: the section requires "New tests, each failing at the base revision" and then, in the same sentence, requires the read to answer "the same runs it answers at the base revision"; an equality arm that compares against base answers passes at base by construction, so it cannot be red there — the identical defect retired for §29 (done_when-1 of r-20261115T170955003258, where both readers returned identical rows at base), which that answer fixed by scoping the failing-first arms and keeping the equality green

findings.reason: s32 measures its failing-first arms against a base that includes s31's landed change, so a section marked landed with an open blocking finding leaves both the base revision and the no-added-failure clause s32 inherits unsettled.
findings.text: plan-section-declarations marks s31 `done` while the plan's own added record for it (plan.html:645) states "broader no-added-failure evidence remains a blocking finding for coordinator adjudication", and no later comment or followup records that adjudication; s31's own done-when still requires that its tests "add no failure against the base on all_debug", which is exactly the evidence the record says is missing
